detail.longDescription: Just read an # article from a # tech # executive # predicting some things # AI # agents are supposed to be able to do within the next ten years. All of them are things that # humans can also do, some of them working alone, some requiring # collaboration . And it occurred to me: a huge number of things we use tech for are # skills we can # develop for ourselves and, having # developed them, our # lives are # richer for it. Many of these skills we so freely abandon don't even require particularly much # effort to cultivate, but require only steering our # attention in simple ways. Lacking these skills and ability to direct attention, # life tends to seem # dull or # boring , and the same # companies who have sold us the means not to have to # learn anything offer up something to consume to fill the void. And then, if we take the offer, we are # hooked twice. And in the case of # chatbots , if we're "collaborating" with a # machine , we rob ourselves of the # joys , # challenges , and # insights of real human collaboration. There is obviously a short-term # benefit here for the people who have not yet learned the skills they need, but in the long term it quickly becomes a problem of # dependency . And it # isolates us besides.
